svg.title: Pedestrian multimodal token prediction architecture diagram
svg.desc: Editable native SVG reconstruction. Inventories: left region contains an example video scene, skeleton sequence, language caption, an input token column labeled T, and a legend. The top blue frame contains three modality projection blocks, token/drop columns, and a fusion encoder. The lower yellow frame contains EMA target projections, target token/drop columns, and three target encoders. The upper right orange frame contains hidden fused tokens H, a branching connector, query/mask tokens Qm, three predictor heads, and prediction tokens y^p. The lower right region contains target tokens Y^t, arrows to three MSE Loss boxes, and matching colored feedback arrows from predictions.

g.desc: Origin objects are the video/photo, skeleton sequence, and text caption; the token column to their right is aligned vertically and drives colored arrows into the encoders.
Within f01, projection blocks at left feed a vertical token/drop column E^f and then the large Fusion Encoder on the right. Basis is horizontal alignment by modality rows.

Within f03, three projection blocks align horizontally to modality-specific target encoders. Token/drop column E^t sits between projections and target encoders. Basis is row-wise symmetry with the top module, connected by EMA.
Within f02, hidden representation tokens H branch to three predictors; query/mask tokens Qm are placed above the predictor stack. The three predictor rows output y^p tokens to the right.
Target tokens Y^t point into modality-specific MSE Loss boxes from the left. Predictions y^p connect by colored orthogonal paths into the same losses from the right, preserving one loss per modality.
